Definition: remote, literally or figuratively, of place or time; specifically, precious; often used adverbially (with preposition)
BiblicalUsage: Rachiyq is far off, remote — in Aramaic, the language of the empire's letters. Darius wrote to Tatnai, governor beyond the river, 'be ye far from thence,' and let the work of the house of God alone.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that the far-off governor was told to stay far off: God set a boundary around His house, and even the empire had to keep its distance.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
